verses.text: The LORD said to Moses,
"Command the people of Israel to send out of the camp anyone who has a serious skin disease, anyone who has a flow from the body, and anyone who is unclean from touching a dead body.
Send out both men and women. Put them outside the camp, so that they do not make the camp unclean, because I live among my people there."
The people of Israel did this. They sent them outside the camp, just as the LORD had told Moses.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell the people of Israel: When a man or woman does wrong to another person in any way, they are being unfaithful to the LORD, and that person is guilty.
He must admit the sin he has done. He must pay back in full what he owes for the wrong, add one fifth more, and give it to the person he wronged.

But if that person has died and has no close relative to receive the payment, the payment belongs to the LORD and must be given to the priest. This is in addition to the ram the priest offers to make the guilty person right with God.
All the special holy gifts that the people of Israel bring to the priest belong to him.
Each person's holy gifts are his own to give, but whatever is given to the priest belongs to the priest."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: A man's wife may go astray and be unfaithful to him.

She may have sexual relations with another man, and her husband does not know about it. She has made herself unclean, but it is kept secret, there is no witness against her, and she was not caught in the act.

Or a feeling of jealousy may come over her husband, and he may suspect his wife, and she really has made herself unclean. Or a feeling of jealousy may come over him and he suspects his wife, even though she has not made herself unclean.

In either case, the man must bring his wife to the priest. He must also bring an offering for her: about one and a half kilograms of barley flour. He must not pour oil or put incense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, an offering to bring a hidden wrong to light.
The priest will bring the woman forward and have her stand in front of the LORD.
He will put some holy water in a clay jar, and take some dust from the floor of the Holy Tent and put it into the water.

The priest will have the woman stand in front of the LORD. He will loosen her hair and put the grain offering for jealousy in her hands, the offering that brings a wrong to light. The priest himself will hold the bitter water that brings a curse.

Then the priest will make the woman take an oath. He will say to her, 'If no other man has slept with you, and you have not gone astray and made yourself unclean while married to your husband, may this bitter water that brings a curse not harm you.
But if you have gone astray while married to your husband, and made yourself unclean by sleeping with a man other than your husband...'
Here the priest will make the woman take the oath of the curse, and say to her, 'may the LORD make your people use your name in curses and oaths, by making your womb shrivel and your belly swell.
May this water that brings a curse go into your body and make your belly swell and your womb shrivel.' And the woman must say, 'Amen. So be it.'
The priest will write these curses on a scroll and then wash the words off into the bitter water.
He will make the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and the water will go into her and cause bitter pain.
The priest will take the grain offering for jealousy from the woman's hands, wave it in front of the LORD, and bring it to the altar.
He will take a handful of the grain offering as the part that is remembered and burn it on the altar. After that he will make the woman drink the water.

If she has made herself unclean and been unfaithful to her husband, then when she drinks the water that brings a curse, it will go into her and cause bitter pain. Her belly will swell and her womb will shrivel, and her name will be used in curses among her people.
But if the woman has not made herself unclean and is pure, she will not be harmed, and she will be able to have children.
This is the teaching about jealousy, for when a wife goes astray and makes herself unclean while married to her husband,
or when a feeling of jealousy comes over a man and he suspects his wife. He must have her stand in front of the LORD, and the priest will do all that this teaching says.
The husband will be free from blame, but the woman will carry the blame for her sin."
